📚 DAILY MARKET EDUCATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🌊 ELLIOTT WAVE BASICS — Reading Market Psychology

Elliott Wave Theory maps crowd psychology through five-wave impulse moves and three-wave corrections. Most traders overcomplicate this — focus on the basics first.

The pattern breaks down simply:
- Waves 1, 3, 5 move with the trend (impulse)
- Waves 2, 4 correct against it
- Wave 3 is typically the strongest and longest
- Never can Wave 4 overlap Wave 1 in a healthy impulse

Real Example: SPX call options in August 2026 showed textbook Elliott structure. Wave 1 rallied from 5200 to 5380. Wave 2 pulled back to 5290. Wave 3 exploded to 5610 (strongest move). Wave 4 corrected to 5510. Wave 5 topped at 5720. Premium buyers who entered at Wave 3 start captured the meat of the move.

How to apply this today:
- Count waves on 4-hour charts for swing trades
- Enter on Wave 2 or 4 pullbacks, not Wave 5 extensions
- Use Wave 3 targets for profit-taking on long options
- If Wave 4 overlaps Wave 1, your count is wrong — reassess

PRO TIP: Wave 3 can never be the shortest impulse wave. If your count shows this, you are mislabeling the structure. Recount from a different starting point.


🏦 CENTRAL BANK POLICIES — The Real Market Movers

Central banks control liquidity — the fuel for all markets. When they tighten, risk assets suffer. When they ease, volatility rises and options premiums expand.

Three policy tools you must track:
- Interest rate decisions (directly impact borrowing costs)
- Quantitative easing or tightening (money supply changes)
- Forward guidance (what they signal for future moves)

Real Example: In June 2026, the Fed held rates steady but shifted language to "data-dependent easing bias." VIX call options surged 23 percent in two days as traders priced volatility expansion. Put options on tech indices became expensive as hedging demand spiked.

Current environment check:
- Fed: Neutral stance, watching inflation data closely
- ECB: Dovish tilt, employment concerns rising
- BOJ: Still accommodative, yen weakness continues

Trading around policy announcements:
- Avoid naked short options positions 48 hours before Fed meetings
- Straddle strategies work best during high-uncertainty windows
- Post-announcement, implied volatility crushes hard — sell premium then

SMART MONEY RULE: Central bank days are not for heroes. Professionals reduce position size and widen stops. Amateurs go all-in and get destroyed by whipsaw moves.


💡 THREE DAILY TRADING TIPS

1. Theta Decay Timing
Options lose time value fastest in the final 30 days before expiration. If you are buying calls or puts, go at least 45-60 days out to avoid rapid decay. Sellers should focus on 20-35 day expiration to capture maximum theta burn.

2. Implied Volatility Rank Check
Before entering any options trade today, check IV rank. Above 70 means premiums are expensive — favor selling strategies like credit spreads. Below 30 means options are cheap — favor buying strategies like debit spreads or outright calls and puts.

3. Watch the VIX Term Structure
Contango (future VIX higher than spot) signals calm markets — good for short volatility trades. Backwardation (spot VIX higher than futures) signals fear — time to hedge with protective puts or reduce leverage across all positions.


⚠️ CORRELATION RISK — The Hidden Portfolio Killer

Correlation risk hits when assets you thought were diversified move in lockstep during stress events. Your hedge becomes worthless exactly when you need it most.

The problem: During market panics, correlations spike to 1.0. Your SPY puts, QQQ puts, and IWM puts all become the same trade. You think you have three hedges but really hold one position sized three times.

Real Example: March 2026 banking stress saw crude oil options, equity index options, and even crypto derivatives all dump simultaneously. Traders with "diversified" put spreads across these assets saw correlations jump from 0.4 to 0.95 overnight. Hedges provided only 30 percent of expected protection.

How to protect yourself:
- Stress-test your portfolio assuming 0.9 correlation in crisis
- Use true uncorrelated hedges like gold, treasuries, or currency options
- Never size positions assuming diversification will save you
- Monitor rolling 30-day correlations weekly via options data

When volatility spikes above 25 VIX:
- Reduce total position count by 30 percent minimum
- Increase cash allocation immediately
- Tighten stops on all derivative positions

PRO TIP: If you cannot explain how each position makes money in three different market scenarios (up, down, sideways), you are over-concentrated and correlation-exposed. Cut until you can.
